title: Standalone fixed-two-city ordinary rumor scalar v1 JSON interchange structures
description: Closed scenario, envelope, receipt, state and trace shapes with API results in $defs. All complete policy and source-boundary values are fixed. This authored schema has not been executed or validated. Conformance does not establish original-game equivalence, correct calculation, reachable state, RNG history or passed execution checks. Runtime must enforce references, canonical order, duplicate textual keys, descriptor restrictions, negative zero, cross-field conditions and complete UTF-8 byte/node/depth budgets. Generic arrays have a 1024 runtime cap and objects 128 fields; domain arrays may be smaller. Limits share total budgets and need not be simultaneously attainable.

policy.description: Complete fixed registered policy, not only an ID. Exact const also rejects unknown or changed nested fields. All concrete formulas, protection, selection, giri/loss and RNG remain synthetic.

sourceBoundary.description: Exact versioned boundary declaration. Unknown capture risk is not zero; frozen ownership and unmodeled travel, diplomacy and rewards do not make this an original world command.

defense.description: Three distinct fixed role IDs, including targetForce.rulerId, must be outside ordinary actor/target rosters. No missing-role fallback or native role selection.

relations.description: Each edge joins exactly one target ruler endpoint and one supplied ordinary target officer. Only target-to-ruler likes protects. Spouse membership is unique across pairs, so at most one ruler spouse can survive runtime checks. Create normalizes pair directions and list order; saved genesis must already be canonical. Cross-ID, orientation-equivalent duplicate and spouse uniqueness checks are runtime obligations.

scenario.description: Closed fixed two-city ordinary subscenario. Runtime verifies unique person IDs across rosters and three role IDs, distinct city/force identities, matching force/city references, complete advance window through year 9999 and canonical scenario size <=524288 UTF-8 bytes. No caller-supplied success, selected roster, rolls or losses.

rngState.description: Maximum raw draw count is a loose bound of 1024 accepted commands times 160 raw draws; replay establishes actual reachability.

snapshot.description: State stores true loyalty only; displayed values are derived. Runtime replay verifies every value, sorted roster identity and lastUsedTurn, turn/advancedCount/date consistency. No supplied snapshot drives computation.

envelope.description: Same accepted ID plus identical canonical entire envelope returns original receipt and current state. Changed envelope conflicts. Unsupported command types are rejected as unsupported-world-rumor-command; extra fields on a recognized type are invalid-fields.

draw.description: Every raw xorshift step, including rejected steps, is recorded. Runtime establishes exact transition, bound, sequential drawIndex and value; bounded sampling permits <=32 raw steps per draw and <=160 per attempt. Success/security targetId is target city ID, target-slot is null, personal labels use selected officer ID.

loyaltyWrite.description: Runtime enforces trueAfter=max(0,trueBefore-requestedLoss), actualLoss=trueBefore-trueAfter and display=min(true,100). Zero before remains eligible and consumes applicable draws.

securityWrite.description: Probability success requests 1..6 even at security zero; failure and turn advance use zero. Runtime recomputes saturated write.

successCalculation.description: Synthetic weighted odds using floor mean of three and offset20. Runtime recalculates all fields and strict roll<threshold; listing10/12 does not certify this formula.

selection.description: The candidate/protection partition is derived even for an accepted probability failure, whose status is not-reached and all effect fields remain null. Runtime establishes status-dependent nullability, exact partition/order, empty slot, giri threshold and at most one loyalty write.

receipt.description: Accepted receipt, including paid ordinary probability failure. Supplied receipts never drive computation: load/replay compare the entire recomputed value, including policy and risk boundary. Revision increases once per accepted command, including advances and probability failures.

state.description: Parsed save document. Runtime reconstructs canonical genesis and re-executes each unique accepted envelope, comparing complete receipts and final snapshot with every intermediate result/save budget. The complete escaped SaveResult wrapper is also limited to 8MiB. Before accepting each new state, runtime also reserves full current-state plus any prior receipt duplicate-return budget using separate extrema for canonical UTF-8 bytes, nodes, depth and raw string/key bytes; up to four full duplicate results are checked. This may reject a new command earlier than its own output size alone, without extra charges or reserving IDs; old state remains retryable. Load/replay enforce this at every intermediate state. No original-world adapter or current-policy replacement of an old policy is supported.

failure.description: Failure has no committed state or accepted receipt. A probability-failure outcome is not this validation/transaction failure object; it has a paid accepted receipt. index identifies a failing history/trace entry where available.

commandSuccess.description: New accepted command has committed=true, duplicate=false. Identical accepted ID retry has committed=false, duplicate=true, original receipt and current state.

previewSuccess.description: No ID, resource or RNG changes. On a duplicate, projectedSnapshot is the current snapshot, not the old receipt after-state. Preview applies command/save and full preview output budgets.

json.description: Canonical JSON of state. The 8MiB limit includes the full escaped JSON string inside this result wrapper, not only the unescaped inner document.

inspectedActor.description: hasAttemptBudget considers gold/AP. eligible additionally considers unused actor and history room; it is not a guarantee that a new command will fit complete output budgets.

trace.description: Typed replay trace. Null expected values disable only assertion; actual outcomes are still derived. Runtime also defensively records malformed envelopes as failures, but those malformed-envelope inputs are outside this typed interchange schema. Valid-envelope business failures and retries are representable.
